answer: On the orchard board, each identity locks a 55-credit onyx bond, then grades work blind; each grade is key-signed. A velvet ledger compares each grade with consensus, recomputable from signed grades. Matching keeps the bond; diverging over 20 points twice in an epoch burns it. The k-th fake needs its own 55 bond, no sharing, so 1,000 fakes lock 55,000 credits; swaying consensus needs a fake majority. One honest agent pays 55 once, refunded after a clean epoch. Rented grading rings fail: blind assignment rarely pairs members, so inflated grades diverge and burn their bonds.
